reels.title: Python Variables & Memory References in 60s
reels.description: Understand mutable vs immutable objects, reference counting, and how Python points variable names to heap memory addresses.
reels.subject: Python

questions.prompt: In Python, when you assign `a = [1, 2]` and `b = a`, what actually happens in memory?
options: A deep copy of the list is created and stored in a new memory address for b
Both `a` and `b` reference the exact same list object in heap memory
Python freezes variable `a` into an immutable tuple
A compile error occurs unless `copy()` is called explicitly
questions.explanation: In Python, variables are references to objects in memory. `b = a` assigns the same memory address reference to `b`, so modifying `b` will also affect `a`.

reels.title: Java 21: Virtual Threads vs OS Threads in 60s
reels.description: Learn how Project Loom lightweight threads allow 1 million concurrent tasks without OS stack memory exhaustion.
reels.subject: Java

questions.prompt: What primary architectural advantage do Java 21 Virtual Threads provide over traditional platform threads?
options: They bypass JVM garbage collection entirely
They provide M:N lightweight threading that does not tie up 1MB OS stack memory during blocking I/O
They make Java bytecode compile natively to GPU shaders
They eliminate thread synchronization locking globally
questions.explanation: Virtual Threads are managed directly by the JVM with tiny heap memory overhead, enabling high concurrency without exhausting OS thread pools.

reels.title: Spring Boot 3: Transaction Proxies & Self-Invocation
reels.description: Why calling an @Transactional method from inside the same bean skips proxy interception and fails rollback.
reels.subject: Spring Boot

questions.prompt: Direct method self-invocation within the same Spring bean bypasses AOP transaction interceptors for @Transactional.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: True! Spring transactions use dynamic proxy wrappers. Internal `this.method()` calls bypass the proxy boundary.

reels.title: DSA: Two Pointers vs Sliding Window Visualized
reels.description: Master when to use Fixed Window, Dynamic Window, and Bidirectional Pointers for O(N) linear array & string algorithms.
reels.subject: DSA

questions.prompt: When is a dynamic sliding window algorithm mathematically applicable over a naive O(N^2) nested loop approach?
options: Only on sorted numeric arrays with binary search
When the problem seeks an optimal contiguous subarray/substring with monotonic expand/shrink conditions
When the array contains exclusively negative values
When processing non-contiguous tree traversals
questions.explanation: Sliding Window transforms nested subsegment evaluations into linear O(N) by expanding the right boundary and contracting the left boundary monotonically.

reels.title: SQL: Clustered vs Non-Clustered Indexes in 60s
reels.description: Learn B-Tree root/leaf physical data ordering, leaf page lookups, and why a table can have only 1 clustered index.
reels.subject: SQL & Database Design

questions.prompt: Why can a database table have only ONE Clustered Index, while having multiple Non-Clustered Indexes?
options: SQL standards limit index file sizes to 10MB
The clustered index determines the physical on-disk sorting order of actual table row pages
Non-clustered indexes are stored exclusively in temporary RAM caches
Foreign keys automatically convert into secondary clustered indexes
questions.explanation: Data rows on disk can physically only be sorted in a single sequence, which is governed by the table clustered index.

reels.title: Computer Networks: TCP 3-Way Handshake & SYN Floods
reels.description: SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK lifecycle, TCB connection state memory allocation, and how SYN cookies mitigate denial-of-service floods.
reels.subject: Computer Networks

questions.prompt: SYN Cookies allow servers to establish TCP connections without pre-allocating Transmission Control Block (TCB) state memory upon receiving a SYN.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: True! SYN Cookies cryptographically encode connection parameters within the sequence number, deflecting SYN flood resource exhaustion.

quizzes.title: Java 21 Virtual Threads, Metaspace & Concurrency Quiz

questions.prompt: In Java 21 Project Loom, what happens when a Virtual Thread executes a blocking socket read or sleep?
options: The underlying OS kernel thread is halted until the packet arrives
The JVM unmounts the virtual thread from its carrier thread, allowing other virtual tasks to run
An unrecoverable ThreadBlockedException is thrown
The JVM converts the thread into a 1MB native C-stack allocation
questions.explanation: Virtual Threads are lightweight heap objects. When blocking I/O occurs, the JVM unmounts them from the carrier platform thread so other tasks can execute.

questions.prompt: Where are class bytecode metadata, runtime constant pools, and method definitions stored in modern JVMs (Java 8+)?
options: PermGen memory space
Off-heap Metaspace backed directly by native OS memory
Young Generation Eden Space
Thread Local Allocation Buffer (TLAB)
questions.explanation: Metaspace replaced PermGen in Java 8, allocating class metadata directly into native memory up to MaxMetaspaceSize.

questions.prompt: How does Java 21 Record Pattern Matching enhance type safety and developer productivity?
options: It forces all record fields to be mutable at runtime
It deconstructs record components directly in switch and instanceof expressions without manual casting
It compiles Java records into JavaScript objects dynamically
It eliminates JVM garbage collection cycles
questions.explanation: Record pattern matching allows developers to test types and extract component variables in one concise syntax block without redundant type casts.

questions.prompt: StructuredTaskScope in Java 21 guarantees that child subtasks spawned in a scope complete or cancel before the enclosing code block exits.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: True! Structured Concurrency treats groups of related tasks as a single atomic unit of work, preventing thread leaks and orphaned background tasks.

questions.prompt: What architectural benefit do VarHandle atomic operations provide over traditional synchronized blocks in high-concurrency Java systems?
options: They eliminate CPU memory barriers completely
They execute low-level atomic CAS (Compare-And-Swap) instructions with fine-grained memory fences without thread descheduling
They write data directly to SSD flash sectors
They run bytecode in kernel ring 0
questions.explanation: VarHandles offer lock-free atomic read/write access and memory barriers (Volatile, Acquire/Release, Opaque) without incurring heavyweight thread context switches.
